theory.intro: 12-hour time uses am and pm; 24-hour time uses four digits from $0000$ to $2359$. We can swap between them with a simple rule.
facts: **am** times keep the same hour: $7\!:\!30$ am $= 0730$ (write a leading zero for hours under $10$).
**pm** times (except $12$ pm) add $12$ to the hour: $3\!:\!15$ pm $= 1515$.
steps: For am: keep the hour, add a leading zero if needed.
For pm: add $12$ to the hour (noon stays $12$).
To go back: hours $13$–$23$ are pm (subtract $12$); $00$ is $12$ am.

foundation.solution_text:
The time is am, so keep hour $6$ and add a leading zero.
$6{:}25\text{ am}=0625$

The time is am, so keep hour $11$.
$11{:}40\text{ am}=1140$

$08$ is before $12$, so the time is am.
$0830=8{:}30\text{ am}$

development.solution_text:
Midnight begins a new day at hour $00$.
$12{:}00\text{ am}=0000$

Noon-hour pm times keep hour $12$.
$12{:}35\text{ pm}=1235$

development.question_text: Order $7{:}50$ pm, $0645$ and $12{:}10$ pm from earliest to latest.
A notice gives the same meeting time as $3{:}20$ pm and $1320$. Identify and correct the mismatch.

mastery.question_text: A flight departs at $12{:}05$ am. Write the time in 24-hour notation and explain why $1205$ is incorrect.
mastery.solution_text:
Hour $12$ am becomes $00$.
$12{:}05\text{ am}=0005$
$1205$ means five minutes after noon.

mastery.question_text: Two alarms are set for $12{:}45$ pm and $0045$. Are they set for the same time of day?
mastery.solution_text:
$12{:}45\text{ pm}=1245$
$0045=12{:}45\text{ am}$
They are not the same time; they are $12$ hours apart.

mastery.question_text: A schedule says $10{:}18$ pm, but a clerk records $1018$. Give the correct 24-hour time and describe the error.
mastery.solution_text:
$10+12=22$
$10{:}18\text{ pm}=2218$
The clerk treated a pm time as an am time.
